newsitem.title: UK: Emerging market debt range-bound in mixed trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt range-bound in mixed trade.

text.p: Emerging market debt was range-bound in quiet trade on Thursday with little recovery seen after losses in the New York session, dealers said.
"It is very quiet today, the market is taking a breather," a dealer said.
Sentiment was mixed as to where prices were headed, some said they remained cautious while others said they liked the market.
"Spreads in the Brady world are still pretty tight and I regard this as a bad time to get sucked into the Greenspan rally," BankAmerica analyst Richard Gray said.
"Thailand is in a complete mess and my forecast is that it will be downgraded," he added.
General optimism on Wednesday followed U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's positive semi-annual report on the state of the economy.
While another analyst said: "I'd be a buyer at the lower levels.

"The market seems to be consolidating at an average spread of around just under 400 basis points over U.S. Treasuries of JP Morgan's Brady bond index for all the Brady bonds. A year ago it was at around 800 b.p over.
"On July 9 it reached an all-time low of 368 b.p. Since then it has been a necessary breather and we are ready to start tightening again," he added.
Following the volatile New York session on Wednesday in which Brazilian paper lost ground, dealers said the paper had settled at the lower levels.
Brazilian "C" bonds were bid at 82.75 at 1000 GMT, little changed from the New York close.

There was still some concern in London on talk that Luis Eduardo Magalhaes might resign his position as whip of the lower house of Brazil's Congress. -- Hayley Pienaar, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7718
